data.content_ref: inline:The problem asks two direct questions: (1) what precisely distinguishes an idempotent operation from a safe one, drawing on published definitions, and (2) which of the TWO properties an append-only event log requires of its writers to survive at-least-once delivery. SRC_001 evades both. Its definitions array is empty — it provides no published definitions at all, ignoring the explicit instruction to ground the distinction in published definitions. It then declares the safe/idempotent distinction a 'false dichotomy' and proposes a 'composite' of safe transport plus idempotent payload, refusing to answer 'which of the two.' The standard answer to (2) is that an append-only log requires writers to be SAFE: retrying an append must not corrupt replay determinism, and the log survives at-least-once delivery because duplicate appends are harmless (the log deduplicates or replay is order-deterministic regardless). By reframing as 'exactly-once semantics at the protocol level,' SRC_001 misstates the problem — the question concerns surviving at-least-once delivery, not achieving exactly-once — and substitutes an unrequested composite for the discriminating answer the problem demands.
